\[
g(x, y) = \frac{1}{2\pi \sigma_x \sigma_y} \exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x'^2}{\sigma_x^2} + \frac{y'^2}{\sigma_y^2}\right)\right) e^{\,i\,2\pi x' / \lambda}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\lambda\): The wavelength in pixels
- \(\theta\): The angle
- \(\sigma_x, \sigma_y\): The Gaussian sizes along the wave and along the stripes

Here x' = x cos theta - y sin theta and y' = x sin theta + y cos theta. The y axis points down, so theta turns counterclockwise on screen. sigma_x is Sigma and sigma_y is Sigma divided by the aspect ratio. The real part of g is a cosine wave and the imaginary part a sine wave. The image is correlated with both, and the magnitude is the length of the complex result. The kernel size and scale follow scikit-image, which convolves, so its imaginary part has the opposite sign.
